stem: Following the intervention, James’ breathing improves and the noises cease. Before moving on in your assessment, which one of the following adjuncts would be beneficial?
explanation: In the trauma primary survey, adjuncts to the ABCDE approach include high-flow oxygen to support oxygenation after airway and breathing are addressed. Nasogastric tube insertion is not the immediate adjunct here and may be deferred if basal skull fracture is suspected. Removing jewellery and cleaning wounds are not priorities before completing the primary survey.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: Trauma care prioritises ABCDE resuscitation; high-flow oxygen is an appropriate adjunct once breathing has been stabilised.

optionExplanations.A: Not the immediate adjunct in the primary survey; airway/aspiration considerations may also make this inappropriate early in assessment.
optionExplanations.B: Not a priority during the primary survey.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. High-flow oxygen is a useful adjunct after improving breathing in a traumatised child.
optionExplanations.D: Not relevant before completing the primary survey and resuscitation priorities.

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
